oracle_provenance: Shannon-Nyquist sampling theorem, standard textbook signal processing; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded sampling-rate criterion check for a declared dataset; not a spectral measurement of actual aliasing.

cases.question: Does the standard 44.1 kHz audio sample rate satisfy the Nyquist criterion for full-band 20 kHz content?
When the sample rate is far below twice the declared signal bandwidth, is that flagged as an aliasing risk?
Must a non-positive sample rate be rejected rather than producing an undefined Nyquist frequency?
At exactly twice the maximum signal frequency (the theorem's own equality boundary), does the criterion still count as satisfied rather than being treated as a violation?
